author: Inside Edition
description: Lindsey Isaacs got the shock of her life when cops showed up at her door, telling her she was involved in a car crash that left three people dead. Police said they'd identified the Florida woman via Flock camera footage. But the cops were wrong. It was a case of mistaken identity. Lindsey tells Inside Edition's Steven Fabian she was arrested, and then spent 13 days in a jail cell.
title: Police Use of Flock Camera Mistakenly Identified Woman Who Was Then Locked Up

author: Inside Edition
description: During their 36 years of marriage, Tom and Diane Keenan have done most things together. Unfortunately for the Michigan couple, that also included having simultaneous heart attacks. When Tom went into cardiac arrest after a recent walk, Diane began CPR and called 911. Then she started to feel unwell.  As Inside Edition's Alison Hall explains, Diane was having a stress-induced heart attack.
title: Couple Have Simultaneous Heart Attacks

author: Inside Edition
description: What was lurking behind the walls of this home in Italy? Authorities say more than 3 million euros in cash. CNN reports military agents raided an apartment in Naples, arresting 34 people and discovering a hidden jackpot worth about $3.6 million US dollars. Video shows officers pulling stacks of bank notes from walls, closets and under floor tiles. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: $3.6 Million Cash Found In Walls And Floors Of Home In Italy

author: Inside Edition
description: When this skunk was in need of help, it went to the right place. The Reno Police Department says it showed up at their main station, despite having a jar stuck on its head. One brave officer decided to take on the case. Dancing around the skunk, wielding a shovel, the officer looked for the perfect opportunity to make a move. Of course, one false step and he would get sprayed. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Cop Helps When Skunk Shows Up To Police Station With Head Stuck In Jar

author: Inside Edition
description: Police in Florida say this U-Haul truck was in possession of stolen, high-priced items: expensive LEGO sets. The Nassau County Sheriff says it was pursuing a man known to them as the 'LEGO Bandit.' They say he was responsible for three incidents in that county where retailers reported thefts of the popular toy brand. They say he was spotted twice at a Target where he allegedly loaded up a cart with LEGO boxes and left through an emergency exit. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Deputies Arrest 'LEGO Bandit' Who Fled In A U-Haul Truck
